Resolves #19638

The multi-window post's first diagram now draws the update triangle the engine runs:
1. The App Worker sends vdom + vnode trees to the VDom Worker.
2. The VDom Worker sends deltas + the new vnode to the component's window.
3. That window's main thread applies them and forwards the reply to the App Worker.

The post also opens for a reader who has never heard of Neo.mjs: a new title, a short subtitle that says what Neo.mjs is, and the 13.2 film as its first image.

Evidence: L2 (both diagrams rendered in the local Portal and in GitHub's renderer at this head) → L2 required. No residual.

## Title and subtitle

- **Title:** "A web app that lives outside its windows." The hook is the post's own thesis, and "Neo.mjs" waits for the subtitle (#13383's cold-reader rule). It passes the blog guide's title test (§3): no "Your …", no comparison, no brag.
- **Subtitle** (the bold line, for Medium's subtitle field): "Neo.mjs, an open-source multi-threaded application engine, can move a web app out of its windows, into one SharedWorker they all share. A panel pulled out onto a second screen is still the same live object."
  - "Can", because `useSharedWorkers` is opt-in.
  - "The same live object" is what the tests assert on both legs: the pop-out (`DockTearOutDefaultRoute.spec.mjs`, "the live pane arrives with its draft") and the return (#19292).
- The old 90-word standfirst is now the opening paragraph, unchanged.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 triangle | Each edge maps to source: ① `Neo.vdom.Helper.updateBatch` (`src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:429`); ② the `{deltas, updateVdom, vnodes}` reply (`src/vdom/Helper.mjs:907`), which Main intercepts (`src/worker/Manager.mjs:542`); ③ `handleDomUpdate` forwards it after the animation-frame apply (`Manager.mjs:426`). Both workers are SharedWorkers under constant names (`Manager.mjs:263-265`). No App Worker → window delta edge remains. |
| AC-2 title/subtitle | See "Title and subtitle" above. |
| AC-3 film | The cover is wrapped in a link to `watch?v=KESyjFmOz0k`, plus a Markdown watch link. It uses the release notes' Portal-safe shape, since the Portal wraps every `<img>` in a `div`, which a `<p>` cannot hold. The cover loads at 1672×941. The watch line discloses the synthesized narration, as the series' other film blocks do, and links the take record. |
| AC-4 render | Local Portal at `#/news/blog/blog/a-workspace-that-can-leave-its-window`: 2 `flowchart-v2` SVGs, nodes in triangle order (App left, VDom top, Main right). GitHub's blob view of this branch: 2 Mermaid frames, same layout. |
| AC-5 blog.json | Parses, and `name` equals the H1 (scripted check). `id` and `path` are unchanged. |
| AC-6 cross-family review | Requested on this PR. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **Diagram shape.** A first draft drew the windows as a subgraph and pointed edges at it. Mermaid then laid the cycle out right to left and clipped the VDom Worker. One main-thread node that names the windows keeps the triangle readable, in plain syntax.
- **Main's relay.** The arrows are logical sends, as in `OffTheMainThread.md` and `WorkerArchitecture.md`. No MessageChannel joins the App and VDom Workers, so Main also relays the request leg; the diagram leaves that out.
- **Release notes.** They still link the post as "A workspace that can leave its window". They are a released artifact, and the URL is unchanged.

The render receipts are in the AC table. `check-ticket-archaeology`, `check-relative-links` (248 links) and `check-file-sizes` pass on this head.
